# Professional experience

For the complete career timeline and official role titles, see my [LinkedIn profile](https://www.linkedin.com/in/brunjm/). The overview below emphasises the different engineering environments and the technical transitions that connect them. It is a thematic summary rather than a replacement for the dated employment history.

My path spans research-laboratory work, startup/product development, software consulting in an ESN, and software-vendor environments at Talend and Qlik. This range has required adapting both the problem-solving approach and the technology stack to the context.

## Research and scientific modelling

**Context:** research-laboratory and thesis work, including work associated with Cemagref.

**Scientific scope:** applied mathematics, partial differential equations, numerical modelling, fluid mechanics, atmospheric dispersion, and environmental processes including infiltration-related questions.

**Methods and technology:** scientific modelling and numerical simulation; SURFEX–TEB and Fortran are part of this research-oriented technical background.

**Evidence:** the [2006 paper on generalised similarity and reduced-complexity modelling](https://comptes-rendus.academie-sciences.fr/mecanique/articles/10.1016/j.crme.2006.06.007/) and the [2008 chapter on reduced-order modelling of dispersion](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-1-4020-8758-5_14). A separate [public-health exposure report](https://www.santepubliquefrance.fr/sites/default/files/rdd/document/82748_9958-9958-ps.pdf) lists Jean-Marc Brun among participants but does not specify an individual role.

## Startup and product development — Beotic / EP

**Context:** startup/product-oriented software work.

**Technology areas:** ActionScript, PHP, front-end development, and BPM (business process management).

This experience adds a product and workflow perspective to the scientific background: implementing user-facing functionality and business processes, not only developing analytical or numerical methods.

## Software consulting / ESN — ASI

**Context:** software delivery in a consulting-services environment.

**Technology areas:** JavaScript and Java.

The consulting context requires adapting to project-specific architectures, integration boundaries, client needs, and delivery constraints. It complements research-oriented work with application-development and systems-integration experience.

## Software-vendor environments — Talend and Qlik

### Talend

**Technology areas:** Java, Spring Boot, Scala, AWS, and Kubernetes.

This environment adds enterprise software, backend services, distributed/cloud deployment, and platform-level engineering to the wider technical profile.

### Qlik

**Context:** five years of Data Science work in the Qlik/Talend lab.

**Technology areas:** Python, Amazon Bedrock, and Amazon SageMaker.

**Work areas:** data analysis and statistics, classical machine learning, LLM/NLP and generative AI, experimentation, benchmarks, model evaluation, and Python development/industrialisation.

One industrial project involved benchmarking approaches for detecting hallucinations in language-model outputs. The public description is deliberately limited to the problem, evaluation approach, scope, and transferable findings; internal code, data, architecture details, and other proprietary information are excluded.

## The common thread

Across these contexts, the recurring work is to understand a domain problem, select a method that fits its constraints, implement or integrate a solution, and evaluate whether it behaves as intended. The combination of scientific modelling, software engineering, and Data Science is the main thread—not any single language or framework.
